articles.title: Are Celtic club in regression amid run of six defeats in 10? Pundits have their say
articles.summary: Chris Sutton and Ian McCall weigh in on Celtic after a second league defeat of the season, but manager Martin O'Neill is defiant.
articles.body:
Towards the end of Sunday's Scottish Premiership defeat by Falkirk, Chris Sutton said it was looking like "one of those days" for Celtic. Afterwards, his remarks about Martin O'Neill's side were much more pointed.

"Martin's not going to say it, of course, but the club is in regression, the team is in regression," Sutton stated on Sky Sports.

"They're just not a good functioning team at this moment in time. It's hard to see how Celtic are actually set up and it is a bit off the cuff.

"They're deficient in every area of the team. This current team are miles off it. Where is the plan, what's the strategy?"

There was some mitigation the leader leaders surprise defeat on Sunday - their sixth in 10 matches in all competitions.

Goalkeeper Scott Bain excelled in goal for Falkirk against his former club - as O'Neill acknowledged - and Falkirk dug in when they needed to get over the line.

Impressive Falkirk earn first win over hapless Celtic in 19 years

Latest Celtic news, analysis and fan views

They are still four points clear, but some other stats paint a grim picture for Celtic.

Twenty-four shots to Falkirk's six; nine on target compared to Falkirk's two (their two goals); more than double the possession and almost three times as many touches in the opposition box. Celtic had 14 corners, Falkirk had none.

Former Falkirk manager Ian McCall was in accord with Sutton, and former Rangers striker Kris Boyd, who said he "couldn't see what Celtic were trying to do".

McCall pointed to age and injury taking its toll on on previously peerless performers. "Carter-Vickers, Tierney, McGregor, Forrest - all of them for different reasons aren't quite what they were," he said on Sportsound.

"That happens in football, it's cruel. Whether it's injury or overuse in Callum McGregor's case, I would suggest. Their bodies maybe aren't capable of the levels they once were.

'It will be tough to bounce back from this'

Europe aside, Celtic's season had been rattling along relatively well.

They had bounced back from League Cup and league losses to Rangers with a solid win at Motherwell, a resounding 7-1 victory at home to last season's runners-up Hearts, and a hard-fought 2-1 win from behind at Hibernian.

Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Dundee United turned out to be a missed opportunity to extend their lead at the top and they now face the prospect of Rangers and, indeed, Hearts getting closer should they win their games in hand.

Besiktas in the Europa League are next up, a home game Celtic really need to win to stand any chance of progress in that competition after starting with three defeats.

Former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner said of O'Neill on BBC Radio Scotland that it's been "a brilliant weekend for Rangers", who won their League Cup semi-final with Aberdeen on Saturday.

"They're in the cup final and Celtic getting beat allows them, when they play their game, their extra game, to close the gap.

"That then puts huge pressure on to Celtic with the European game coming up now in midweek also. That is going to be tough for them to bounce back from this."

Of course, O'Neill has seen this all before - fairly recently, in fact. He twice stepped back into the dugout in Celtic's hour of need last season and ultimately led them to a league and cup double.

Indeed, sitting atop the Premiership after 12 games, he was quick to point out in his spiky post-match interview that Celtic are in a better position than at the same stage last season, when they were four points behind leaders Hearts.

"I don't know whether [supporters] are angry," O'Neill told BBC Sport Scotland. "Every single time that Celtic lose a game, people can be angry and frustrated. We come under scrutiny and so we should because this is it, the club is used to winning.

"It's a long season. This time last year, we were in a worse position."

O'Neill was also asked about the amount of changes that had been made to his team of late.

"Why would you not change the team? We have an abundance of games," he replied.

"We're playing European football. We're trying to hold the Scottish flag up, so we have to change. It's hard for the same players to play every single week."

'Plot has been lost' - what the fans say

Alan: Sorry to say, but the plot has been lost. Strange bench selection. Even stranger half time sub. Then we take off our best two midfielders and leave an underperforming captain on the pitch. What is going on??

Imran: I think football has changed too much for O'Neill to be a modern manager. I think he should take a back seat and allow a younger, more ambitious manager to take charge. It would be a shame for his legacy to be tarnished and that's what looks like will happen as no major changes look imminent.

Sean: Very, very Poor. Falkirk deserved the win.

Kevin: Keep the faith Celtic fans... stay strong.

Edward: Dismal display, Johnstone is not in any way superior to Sinisalo, was surprised at Carter Vickers performance. The unthinkable must now be thought. Is Martin O'Neill able to progress this side? If the answer was Forrest, Tounekti and McCowan the question is NOT how to win a football match.

Liam: Enough is enough. This is rapidly turning into a disaster and we need change: from the board to the manager to the coaching staff to the players. So much for quality over quantity.

articles.title: Mourinho: "El árbitro ha estado técnicamente muy bien"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del entrenador del Real Madrid depués del choque ante el Racing
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del entrenador del Real Madrid depués del choque ante el Racing
articles.body: José Mourinho acaba de comparecer en la sala de prensa de El Sardinero para atender a los medios después del duelo Racing-Real Madridr. El técnico portugués ha valorado lo ocurrido en lo que ha sido el regreso del Madrid a Santander después de 15 años. Partido: "Era de 0-4, pero se podía haber complicando. Es una buena victoria en una semana importante". Bellingham y Diomande: "Hay jugadores con más aptitud física y táctica. He visto un equipo muy comprometido. El equipo crece. Debemos marcar más goles. En bloque bajo, el equipo sabe ser compacto. El mensaje de sacrificio es muy positivo". Tecla: "Crecemos. No estamos al 100%. Es un crecimiento progresivo. Entendemos cosas que el primer día no entendíamos. La empatía humana es buena entre nosotros, mis ideas y sus cualidades. Estamos bien. A ver cómo acaba la semana". Las polémicas: "Ellos protestaban todo. Me gusta mucho este estadio. Tiene carácter. No se limitan a venir al cine, a ver un espectáculo. Aquí la afición juega. Pero hay mucha gente que no sabe las reglas, en parte porque cambian mucho. Nunca es penalti de Tchouaméni. A 60 metros no podía verlo, pero al verlo estaba seguro de que el del VAR no estaba dormido. No es penalti. El árbitro ha estado técnicamente muy bien". Equipo: "La confianza es alta. Al fútbol juegan personas y el aspecto emocional cuenta mucho. Cuando las cosas van bien, todo es más fácil. Ahí está el caso de Trent, ha hecho un partido top después de varios partidos sin jugar. Las cosas parecen mejor de lo que son en realidad cuando ganas partidos". El 0-3 y su gesto: "¿Te imaginas que un listo nos pilla y saca rápido? Yo intento ayudar en todo al equipo". Cambios: "He visto de todo, así que de sentenciado, nada. En mi cabeza estaba el partido de Atenas, dejar dentro a gente que no va a ser titular el miércoles. Es el regalo de la Liga. El fútbol español quiere ver que sus equipos ganan. Vamos a ver si con cuatro o cinco cambios podemos hacerlo".

articles.title: Deportivo - Osasuna | Sumar de tres para curar las heridas: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: El conjunto gallego lleva seis jornadas sin ganar y los rojillos no logran vencer lejos de El Sadar desde agosto
articles.summary: El conjunto gallego lleva seis jornadas sin ganar y los rojillos no logran vencer lejos de El Sadar desde agosto
articles.body: Las urgencias de Deportivo y Osasuna, que cierran la undécima jornada, asoman en Riazor. Unos llevan sin ganar desde el mes de septiembre y los otros no lo hacen fuera desde agosto. El abismo está cerca, pero sumar de tres también les acerca a Europa. Por lo tanto, ganar es vital para ambos. El Deportivo lleva una racha de seis jornadas sin conocer la victoria. El técnico no está nervioso y asegura que la cantidad de puntos que llevan los gallegos es buena. “Llevamos unos puntos que son buenos a estas alturas, tenemos que tener una dosis de realidad de la dificultad que tiene Primera División donde cualquier equipo te complica y este lunes tocará sufrir seguro”, expresó en la previa del choque frente a Osasuna. El Dépor buscará el objetivo de no encajar. No hay que olvidar que el conjunto de Hidalgo ha encajado gol en las diez jornadas de Liga (13 goles). “La portería a cero es un mantra, no sólo a nosotros. Llevamos 13 goles en 10 partidos. No es una mala cifra. Hemos encajado en todos y es una evidencia”, expresó. En relación al once Hidalgo volverá a contar con su equipo titular sin las bajas de Aubameyang, Casadó y Ede. También sigue fuera Eddahchouri tras romperse la muñeca. Osasuna espera volver a ganar en Riazor más de 18 años después y así volver a la senda del triunfo a domicilio. Para el conjunto navarro esto es una nueva prueba lejos de El Sadar con la intención de cambiar su dinámica a domicilio y superar uno de los escenarios históricamente más complicados para los intereses rojillos. La victoria frente al Celta en agosto sigue siendo la única alegría rojilla como visitante esta temporada. Desde entonces, cuatro derrotas y 16 goles encajados dibujan una asignatura pendiente que el conjunto navarro necesita empezar a corregir. Nsongo vs. Budimir. El camerunés apura sus minutos de titular fijo a la espera de la vuelta de Aubameyang. De momento, solo un gol en Liga. Todo lo contrario que el croata, indiscutible en Osasuna: siete goles en nueve partidos y vital para el resurgir rojillo.

articles.title: Indignación en el Racing por el penalti señalado a favor del Madrid
articles.standfirst: Una decisión muy cuestionada castiga al Racing, que ya acumula seis penas máximas sufridas en lo que va de temporada
articles.summary: Una decisión muy cuestionada castiga al Racing, que ya acumula seis penas máximas sufridas en lo que va de temporada
articles.body: El Real Madrid abrió el marcador en El Sardinero gracias a un penalti señalado por Munuera Montero por un supuesto agarrón de Prati sobre Mbappé. Las imágenes en la televisión demostraron que el contacto entre el centrocampista italiano y Mbappé es mínimo y no debería haberse señalado penalti. Además Milla Alvendiz, colegiado encargado del VAR, no pudo avisar a Munuera Montero, ya que aunque mínimo, hubo contacto. Plantilla, cuerpo técnico y afición racinguistas estaban indignados por la señalización de la pena máxima. Los cántabros tenían claro la dificultad de vencer al Real Madrid en condiciones normales, por lo que con ayuda arbitral dejaban la misión como imposible. Iván Martín en Dazn tenía claro que no debería haberse pitado penalti. "Le metió Prati un poco el brazo, pero no suficiente, para mí no se debe pitar penalti". Posteriormente el VAR corrigió a Munuera Montero cuando señaló un penalti a favor del Racing por mano de Tchouaméni en el área. El Racing es el equipo de Primera división que más penaltis ha cometido en este Liga con 6. Además de este de Prati sobre Mbappé, el conjunto cántabro cometió 3 frente al Barcelona en el Camp Nou, otro en Bailados frente al Celta y otro más en El Sadar ante Osasuna. De los seis penaltis 5 fueron goles y tan sólo Agirrrezabala pudo parar una pena máxima a Lamine en Barcelona.

articles.title: Arteta reconquista Anfield 14 años después y su Arsenal vuelve a ser líder
articles.standfirst: Un solitario tanto de Havertz en la primera parte salvó para tumbar a un Liverpool que enlazaba cinco victorias consecutivas
articles.summary: Un solitario tanto de Havertz en la primera parte salvó para tumbar a un Liverpool que enlazaba cinco victorias consecutivas
articles.body: Había que remontarse hasta a septiembre de 2012 para rescatar el último triunfo en Premier del Arsenal sobre el tapete de Anfield. Aquel día, Mikel Arteta fue titular y, más de 14 años después, reconquisto el templo 'red' con una ajustada victoria ante el Liverpool de su amigo Iraola —enlazaban cinco triunfos consecutivos— que les permite auparse al liderato en solitario tras los últimos 'pinchazos' del Manchester City. Con Ronald Araújo de vuelta al lateral derecho, Iraola premió el ascenso de Trey Nyoni situándole en el doblete pivote 'red' junto a Mac Allister. En el Arsenal, por su parte, tan sólo repitieron Timber y Havertz respecto a la 'debacle' sufrida en Carabao. Bruno Guimaraes, que falló su penalti frente al Fleetwood, acompañó a Rice y Odegaard en la sala de máquinas, mientras que Tzolis entró directamente al once tras seis partidos fuera por lesión. Una de las mayores señas de intensidad en los respectivos modelos de Iraola y Arteta es la intensidad. El partido arrancó con infinidad de duelos y no estaba permitido pensar a más de dos toques. Con balón, sin embargo, el Arsenal optó por una propuesta más controladora... mientras que el Liverpool no tenía miedo en salir rápido en transición. Fue Rice el primer que se animó a disparar justo cuando se cumplía el primer cuarto de hora. Su remate, lejano, se fue a las nubes. En el reinicio, sin embargo, Alisson metió en un compromiso a Jacquet que permitió al Arsenal atacar en posicional plantado en la frontal rival. El propio Rice hizo un esfuerzo titánico para doblar a Madueke y metió un envío tenso que Havertz embocó en el segundo palo. No se vino abajo el Liverpool... ni tampoco Anfield. La presión fue en aumento y Barcola empezó a hacer bastante daño por izquierda. De sus botas nació un centro lateral que Isak no llegó a cabecear. Le agarró lo justo Timber, que se jugó el penalti. También estuvo valiente Raya para, poco después, evitar que el sueco rematase un saque de esquina peinado por Van Dijk. Entre medias, Havertz se quedó con la miel en los labios hasta en dos ocasiones. Se marchó ciertamente frustrado el Liverpool al túnel de vestuarios. Y es que, a poco más de cinco minutos para el descanso, Wirtz probó suerte con una falta que superó a Raya... pero se acabó estrellando contra el larguero. Mac Allister, además, mandó arriba un 'cabezazo' franco desde el corazón del área a centro de Kerkez. No suele ser habitual. Pero sufrió el Arsenal a la hora de defender ese tipo de envíos. No quería el Liverpool que se diluyese la efervescencia con la que acabó una primera parte en la que tuvo un 60% de posesión, tocó 30 balones en el área rival... pero no fue capaz de encontrar portería en ninguno de sus ocho disparos. Isak se apuntó la primera del segundo acto, pero su 'zurdazo' se marchó bastante desviado. No esperó Iraola a que se cumpliese la hora de partido para comenzar a recargar pilas... dando entrada a un Dominik Szoboszlai que se había perdido los tres últimos partidos. Quien le dejó su sitio junto a Mac Allister fue Nyoni, que firmó una actuación notable en su primera titularidad en la Premier aportando claridad desde los primeros pases. La asfixiante presión del Liverpool, lejos de minimizarse, transmitía la sensación de ir a más. Reacción Arteta reclamando la presencia de un 'desactivador' como Lewis-Skelly... aunque entró 'frío' y una pérdida en su primera acción abrió la puerta a una transición 'red'. Iraola, por su parte, metió todavía más madera con Ngumoha. Recuperó cierto control el Arsenal... y también capacidad de amenaza. Van Dijk protagonizó un corte providencial sobre Havertz en boca de gol y, poco después, Alisson sacó una mano dura para mandar a córner un brillante disparo de Tzolis. Había perdido fuelle el Liverpool y, además de Tsimikas, Víctor Muñoz entró como lateral y Koumas para partir por detrás de Isak a falta de 10' para el final. Resistieron los 'gunners' con una línea de cinco atrás y reconquistaron Anfield 14 años después.

articles.title: Freddie James Dies at 89, Legendary Coach Was Portrayed in 'Friday Night Lights' Movie
articles.summary: Legendary high school football coach Freddie James died Thursday at 89 years old, per his obituary.
articles.body:
Legendary high school football coach Freddie James died Thursday at 89 years old, per his obituary .

Mark Heim of AL.com noted James, who coached at Carter high school in Texas, was portrayed in the 2004 Friday Night Lights movie and 2015's Carter High . He was played by Julius Tennon in the Friday Night Lights movie, which was eventually turned into a television show.

He was played by Charles S. Dutton in Carter High .

James won 135 games from 1982 to 1995 with Carter in Dallas and was recognized with a number of awards and honors.

The obituary noted he was recognized with the 1988 Frederick Douglas Award, 1989 Table of Champions, the UIL Hall of Honor, African American Hall of Fame at Fair Park in Dallas, the Prairie View Hall of Fame, the 1958 Championship Hall of Fame, the Atlanta Texas Sports Hall of Fame and the Dallas Independent School District Hall of Fame.

What's more, he won the DISD Coach of the Year eight times during his career.

He coached eight players who reached the NFL, including Jesse Armstead.

Armstead was a five-time Pro Bowler and was named to the All-Pro First-Team during the 1997 campaign for the New York Giants.

articles.title: José Alberto: "Mou dijo que cuando un error le favoreciese lo iba a decir..."
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Racing respondió al portugués en rueda de prensa
articles.summary: El entrenador del Racing
articles.body: José Alberto analizó en rueda de prensa la derrota frente al Real Madrid en El Sardinero. VAR: "Nos da igual lo que nos expliquen, al final no entiendo por qué hay partidos en los que el VAR interviene, otros no, hay acciones que sí, otras no, es lo que puedo decir. Igual que digo esto, digo que la acción que revisan de la mano, el penalti que nos quitan y que lo quitan, para mí está bien interpretado, para eso está el VAR. Pero es que el primer penalti, todos los que somos de fútbol, ves esa acción y es que no pasa absolutamente nada". Polémicas: "El fútbol se puede tocar, lo que no se puede es derribar, no se puede agarrar, pero se puede tocar, entonces eso es lo que me llama la atención y me molesta. Evidentemente nos hemos encontrado con un gran Madrid, con un Madrid que nos ha sometido en la primera media hora y que ha sido mucho mejor que nosotros, pero creo que lo condiciona todo ese primer gol en esa acción del penalti. ¿Y usted le ha preguntado por qué no ha ido a revisarlo desde el VAR? Porque entienden que no es suficiente, de verdad que entienden que no es suficiente, que es lo que me llama la atención, porque hemos visto, hace poco Mou en una rueda de prensa decía que si el VAR estaba de vacaciones, pues hoy posiblemente también". Respuesta a las palabras de Mourinho: "Mourinho dijo en una rueda de prensa que cuando un error le favoreciese lo iba a decir. Poco más puedo decir..." Conversación con Munuera Montero: "No, da gusto, ¿no? Da gusto el poder hablar con un árbitro como lo he hecho con Munuera al término del partido. Para mí aciertan, viendo las imágenes del penalti a favor nuestro que quitan, porque es una jugada que intenta jugar y le pega la mano. Creo que es un acierto del árbitro, pero me llama mucho la atención que en el penalti del 0 a 1 no se revise ese tipo de acciones. Él me da su explicación, él ve penalti claro, pero yo creo que cuando lo vea en casa y me vuelva a encontrar con él, pues posiblemente me dé otra otra versión de lo que de lo que ha ocurrido y de lo que ha visto. Y para eso está el VAR. Para eso está el VAR, es lo que me molesta. Es que tocar a un jugador no es falta ni es penalti ni es absolutamente nada. Tocar a un jugador no es nada, en el fútbol hay contacto. Entonces, no hay agarrón, no hay empujón, no hay absolutamente nada. Entonces, cualquiera de los que estáis aquí creo que habéis tenido la oportunidad de verlo seguramente por imágenes, y cualquiera del fútbol tendrá posiblemente pues la misma opinión que estoy expresando yo. Y bueno, pues Munuera, el árbitro arbitra lo que ve, pero me llama mucho la atención que haya una persona o varias personas en un monitor y no llamen para para revisar esa acción, al igual que lo han hecho en la jugada que era favorable a nosotros y que creo que está bien arbitrada, porque para eso está el VAR".

articles.title: Liverpool v Arsenal player ratings: Whose mistake was costly? Who was the top Gunner?
articles.summary: How Liverpool and Arsenal's players rated in their Premier League match at Anfield, as the champions of the past two seasons went head to head.
articles.body:
Kai Havertz's first-half goal made the difference as Arsenal won at Anfield in the Premier League for the first time since 2012.

Here's how we rated the Liverpool and Arsenal players, and your scores are below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Premier League: Arsenal go top with rare win at Liverpool

Alisson: It was his error - a poor pass out - that led to Havertz giving Arsenal the lead. Made a great save to deny Christos Tzolis but that mistake ultimately proved costly. 4

Ronald Araujo : Made his 12th consecutive start. Battled well as ever but was given a really tough test by Tzolis down Arsenal 's left. 6

Jeremy Jacquet : Shaky in patches but had a decent game on the whole and made a superb tackle after slipping in the second half. 6

Virgil van Dijk : Reliable as ever but will be so disappointed with how easily Liverpool gifted Arsenal the lead. 6

Milos Kerkez : Had a frustrating first half but delivered a lovely cross which Alexis Mac Allister should have headed in. 5

Trey Nyoni : A real show of faith from Andoni Iraola to give the 19-year-old his first Premier League start. Looked a bit nervy early on but grew into the game. 6

Alexis Mac Allister : Constantly involved in the first half but will know that he should have scored when Kerkez found him. 6

Bradley Barcola : Started down his preferred left flank and caused Arsenal plenty of problems, though he is still waiting for a first Premier League goal. 7

Florian Wirtz : Hit the bar with a great free-kick in the first half, but a player with his price tag simply has to do more in big games. 6

Cody Gakpo : Looked lively initially, but Riccardo Calafiori dealt with him very well. Could have had a penalty, but the appeal was waved away by Andy Madley. 5

Alexander Isak : Got in some good positions but couldn't find the net. Unlucky not to get a penalty when his shirt was pulled by Timber. 5

Szoboszlai (on 59, Nyoni): Back after a spell on the sidelines. 6

Ngumoha (on 67, Gakpo): Didn't get on the ball as much as he would have liked. 5

Munoz (on 82, Araujo): Tried to make an impact with his pace.

Koumas (on 82, Wirtz): Thrown on to add some energy.

Tsimikas (on 82, Kerkez): Didn't have much luck down the left.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Endo, Gravenberch.

David Raya: Made a good clearance after a ball was played through the Arsenal defence in the first half. The usual assured performance from the goalkeeper. 7

Jurrien Timber: Involved in a very good battle with Barcola and had to deal with a lot of attacks down the right side. Perhaps lucky to not give away a penalty for a shirt pull on Isak. 7

Ezri Konsa: Continued his recent good form and was solid in the middle of the Arsenal back four. 8

Gabriel Magalhaes: Dealt with the threat of Isak and led the Arsenal backline. 8

Riccardo Calafiori: Not allowed to attack as much as usual but a solid defensive performance from the left-back. 8

Declan Rice: The midfielder provided the assist for Havertz's goal and was Arsenal 's best player. His energy in midfield was a big reason the Gunners won the game. 8

Bruno Guimaraes: An all-action display and involved in the move for the Arsenal goal. Subbed just after an hour. 6

Martin Odegaard: Won the ball back which started the move for the Arsenal opener. 6

Noni Madueke: Heavily involved in the opening goal as he started after shaking off a knock. Tired as the game went on. 6

Christos Tzolis: The winger's first start since September after injury and provided a threat from the left. Forced Alisson into an excellent save with a curling effort. 6

Kai Havertz: Scored the only goal of the game, which he needed after a difficult couple of matches. Put himself about and linked the play. 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly (on 62, Guimaraes): Came on and helped to calm the game down for Arsenal as Liverpool pushed for an equaliser. 7

Piero Hincapie (on 84, Tzolis): Brought on to see out the win. 6

Viktor Gyokeres (on 84, Havertz): Introduced to provide a threat behind the backline. 6

Merino (on 88, Odegaard): Added defensive strength for the closing minutes.

articles.body:
It's now been two difficult seasons for Kylian Mbappe in terms of team success at Real Madrid , but he has been unmatched in La Liga on a personal level when it comes to scoring goals.

The 27-year-old has finished top of the league's goalscoring chart after each of his two seasons in the Spanish capital, creating a divide between collective silverware and individual achievement.

Mbappe is the overwhelming favorite to finish atop the charts for a third consecutive campaign, especially now that Madrid have bolstered their attack even further by spending big on Yan Diomande .

He will be challenged by Clasico foes Barcelona , who are hoping that Lamine Yamal and Raphinha will be boosted by big-money additions in Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi .

The Sporting News is tracking the Golden Boot race in La Liga all season long, right until the final matchday on May 30.

Updated ahead of Athletic Club vs. Real Sociedad on Sunday, November 1.

Favorites, odds to win La Liga Golden Boot 2026/27

As two-time defending champion, Kylian Mbappe is the clear runaway favorite to win the Pichichi trophy in the 2026/27 La Liga season.

Nobody else is even close to Mbappe, who sports negative odds to begin the campaign at 4/7 to lead the league in goal scoring.

The next two individuals on the list are both from Barcelona, as Lamine Yamal and Raphinha are both considered the likely challengers, but those two often create for others as much as scoring themselves, so it's hard to see them challenging a world-class scorer like Mbappe.

For the second straight year, Kylian Mbappe won the Pichichi trophy as the top goal scorer in La Liga.

The Real Madrid star topped the charts by two over Verdat Muriqi of Mallorca , even though he missed some time through the second half of the season due to injury.

Mbappe gave himself enough of a lead with a scorching hot first-half, finding the back of the net in 18 of his first 22 appearances in La Liga action.

Below is a list of the most regular winners of La Liga's top goal scorer throughout the history of the prize.

Lionel Messi holds the record for the most goals in La Liga history (474 goals) and also boasts the most Golden Boot prizes in the competition.

The award these days is known as the Pichichi, named in honour of former Athletic Club striker Rafael "Pichichi" Moreno.

articles.title: Bundesliga Player Ratings | Eintracht Frankfurt 3-1 Hamburg
articles.summary: In an immediate rematch between two tradition-rich Bundesliga clubs who met in the DFB-Pokal five days earlier, Adi Hütter’s Eintracht Frankfurt defeated Mer...
articles.body:
In an immediate rematch between two tradition-rich Bundesliga clubs who met in the DFB-Pokal five days earlier , Adi Hütter's Eintracht Frankfurt defeated Merlin Polzin's Hamburg by the exact same scoreline as in the cup. A complete team performance from the German Eagles at their Waldstadion lifted Hessen's SGE to eighth place in the table following a 3-1 victory, their third Bundesliga win of the season. History was also made when, as promised , Hütter introduced 16-year-old prodigy Niko Ilicevic late in the encounter. At 16 years and one day, Ilicevic equalled Youssoufa Moukoko's record as the youngest player in Bundesliga history.

The hosts noticeably carried some momentum from Tuesday's Pokal victory into the encounter, making regular incursions into HSV's penalty area in the opening minutes. An interesting short corner design in the fifth minute concluded with Can Uzun putting the ball just wide. A little over a minute later, Younes Ebnoutalib stung the palms of HSV keeper Daniel Heuer Fernandes after a Miro Muheim turnover in the back ranks led to a flash-fire scoring chance directly in front of goal. One certainly sensed that the early momentum would soon be reflected on the scoresheet.

One-way traffic eventually yields opener

Eintracht's relentless attacking waves finally produced the 1-0 in the 10th minute. The resurgent Uzun played in Fares Chaïbi on the left with a sparkling run and through ball. Chaïbi's square ball, intended for the onrushing Ebnoutalib, took an unfortunate deflection that left Heuer Fernandes unable to intercept. HSV defender Warmed Omari couldn't adjust to the deflection either and inadvertently steered the ball into his own net. As fluky as the match's first goal was, it certainly counted as a well-earned tally for the superior hosts.

Double Brassier mistake enables Hamburg to equalize

The Hanseatic visitors had barely arrived in the match, yet were able to draw level just four minutes later with their first promising attack. Two defensive errors from SGE center-back Lilian Brassier in the same sequence led to the equalizer. Brassier first botched a touch, allowing Hamburg's Miro Muheim to drive deeper into the area. The defender then sent a poor clearance of Muheim's cross onto the foot of Albert Grønbaek. The Danish attacker alertly laid the ball off for Terem Moffi, who coolly slid home the 14th-minute 1-1.

A captivating contest heads into the break level

An immensely entertaining first half somehow drew to a close without any additional goals. Exquisite dribbling work from Grønbaek and David Møller Wolfe produced an eye-catching chance for HSV in the 26th minute. At the other end, Doan (28th) and Chaïbi (31st) broke through to create excitement in front of the HSV net. Albert Sambi Lokonga (38th) and Muheim (39th) then earned their respective rounds of applause from the visiting supporters with another pair of Hamburg chances. Eintracht drew two saves out of Heuer Fernandes with headed efforts in the 45th minute of first-half stoppage time and a minute later.

A 1-1 scoreline at halftime felt right, even if the Hessian hosts enjoyed a slight optical advantage.

The seats at the Waldstadion weren't fully repopulated after the halftime break before the hosts retook the lead. Two SGE players who had committed their fair share of mistakes in the opening 45 both played important roles in the 47th-minute 2-1. After Ebnoutalib dug out a 46th-minute corner, Brassier headed the subsequent delivery on target. Raphael Onyedika quickly pounced on the rebound, beating Jordan Torunarigha to the loose ball and scoring his first goal for his new Bundesliga club. Uzun nearly added to the lead four minutes later with a fine effort from distance.

A splendid goal that could have put the match beyond the visitors' reach in the 62nd minute was disallowed for a marginal offside position. More excellent dribbling work from Uzun unleashed Ansgar Knauff on the right. An inch-perfect cross from the halftime substitute, who had replaced Keita Kosugi, was then stroked home by Chaïbi. Replays nevertheless confirmed that Knauff was narrowly ahead of the HSV defensive line upon receiving the pass. Both players missed out on a well-deserved opportunity to get their names on the scoresheet.

Regensburg's German-Turkish phenom showed no interest in the fact that his earlier work had been chalked off and continued to play like a man possessed. A top-notch midfield ball win from the 20-year-old in the 69th minute eventually produced the 3-1. Uzun embarked on a scorching individual run, deftly drawing defenders toward him before picking out an onside Ebnoutalib for the goal that would decide the game. Electrified by their two-goal cushion, Eintracht poured it on. Only the crossbar denied Chaïbi six minutes later. Doan and newly introduced substitute Jonathan Burkardt also managed to get quality looks at goal.

Noah Atubolu shines, Niko Ilicevic makes history

Hamburg threatened to claw a goal back late on, but SGE summer acquisition Noah Atubolu responded with a pair of strong saves shortly before second-half stoppage time. At the beginning of added time, Hütter and captain Robin Koch both received bookings for protesting that they weren't being permitted to introduce Ilicevic. The 16-year-old eventually made it onto the pitch and equalled Moukoko's Bundesliga age record, even managing, to the delight of the crowd, to get two shots away before the full-time whistle.

GGFN Bundesliga Player of the Match: Can Uzun (9)

Eintracht Frankfurt's Can Uzun made an emphatic case for a return to regular first-team football in Sunday's 3-1 victory over Hamburger SV. The 20-year-old attacking midfielder delivered an influential performance in his first Bundesliga start since Matchday 5, providing an assist and helping orchestrate Frankfurt's attacking play.

Uzun's early-season struggles made the display particularly noteworthy. The Turkish international had received disappointing individual grades in four of his previous five Bundesliga starts, with his brace against Mainz on Matchday 3 accounting for his only two league goals of the campaign. As Get German Football News examined in its Frankfurt preseason tactical preview , questions surrounding Uzun's defensive responsibilities and suitability for Adi Hütter's preferred system had already emerged during the summer. His two-goal performance against Mainz subsequently demonstrated what the youngster could offer when provided with greater attacking freedom.

Against Hamburg, Uzun registered 77 touches, completed 84 percent of his 51 attempted passes, and contributed three shots with a combined xG of 0.20. His assist carried an xA value of 0.49. The midfielder also covered an impressive 12.02 kilometres in 89 minutes, providing evidence of his considerable involvement throughout the encounter.

Uzun has now done a spectacular job from the No. 10 slot in two consecutive matches.

articles.title: From Barcelona’s captain to Anfield’s cult hero: The blooming Ronald Araujo-Liverpool love affair
articles.summary: There is something wonderful about watching Ronald Araujo celebrate a goal at Anfield.On October 20, Liverpool were trailing Villarreal 2-1. Having already b...
articles.body:
There is something wonderful about watching Ronald Araujo celebrate a goal at Anfield.

On October 20, Liverpool were trailing Villarreal 2-1. Having already been two goals down, Andoni Iraola's men were desperate to get back on level terms before half-time.

Minutes into first-half stoppage time, Rio Ngumoha picked up the ball and delivered a teasing cross towards the far post.

The Reds youngster put a bit more on the ball than he should have, but Araujo refused to give up on it, arriving behind the defenders and heading home Liverpool's equaliser .

Then came the moment that told the bigger story. The former Barcelona defender's momentum carried him into the Anfield Road stand, where he found himself among jubilant Liverpool supporters.

For a few seconds at Anfield that night, the boundaries between a footballer and a fan disappeared. Arms reached towards him. Strangers embraced him.

Liverpool eventually won the game 4-3, but the celebration felt more exhilarating than any of the seven goals scored on Merseyside that night.

Araujo has been an unexpected hit at Liverpool.(Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images)

For Barcelona supporters, watching it all u nfold stirred rather complicated emotions. A defender who struggled to convince towards the end of his time in Catalonia is becoming one of the most loved players among Liverpool supporters.

Anfield is falling in love with the Araujo Barcelona once knew

Football supporters often recognise passion before they notice technical ability.

Sometimes, all it takes to win over a crowd is someone willing to put his body somewhere others would hesitate to put a foot.

Against Brighton & Hove Albion last weekend, Araujo provided the perfect example of this. Having already gone to ground, he somehow managed to push the ball away from Maxim de Cuyper's path with his head.

Later in the game, a thunderous, full-blooded, clean challenge on Malick Yalcouye brought another enormous roar from the Anfield crowd. They celebrated these Araujo interventions like goals.

His performance in the 2-0 victory over the Seagulls earned him the Premier League Player of the Matchweek award. Araujo registered eight clearances and won every ground and aerial duel he contested.

Jamie Carragher, a Reds legend, had already called Araujo a cult hero back in September, just weeks into his Liverpool career.

Yet the most interesting part of this growing affection is how it feels like déjà vu . Barcelona supporters remember this version of Araujo.

The defender who threw himself into challenges, chased down seemingly unstoppable attackers and made defending look like an art.

Those qualities once made him indispensable at the Spotify Camp Nou . Now, 1,000 miles away, they are once again making him indispensable to another fanbase.

The complicated ending to Araujo's Barcelona story

It is easy to forget how quickly Araujo's fortunes changed at Barcelona.

The Uruguayan arrived in 2018 and rose through the reserves to eventually become a first-team captain for the Catalan club.

His battles with Vinicius Jr. in El Clasico matches over the years became one of the defining images of La Liga at that point.

Araujo was involved in the Liverpool squad that lost to Arsenal. (Photo by Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

In a team filled with technically gifted players, Barcelona embraced Araujo's physicality like a breath of fresh air.

He was supposed to be a part of the future. Even as recently as January 2025, Barcelona extended his contract until 2031.

However, Hansi Flick's arrival changed Araujo's fortunes. The German manager got Barça playing a high defensive line that required precise positioning and coordination.

For all of Araujo's brilliance, he struggled with those demands. His performances left a lot to be desired. The red card against Chelsea was the straw that broke the camel's back.

Araujo subsequently took a sabbatical from the sport to prioritise his mental health. He returned and put in some decent performances without ever looking like the player of old.

By the following summer, Barcelona and Flick were prepared to let him leave. It is these circumstances that make his Liverpool resurgence so intriguing.

It's not as if Araujo suddenly learned how to defend. He just regained his confidence in a setting where his strengths are being celebrated again.

A different role, a familiar kind of freedom

There is a certain irony to Araujo's success under Andoni Iraola because it isn't as if the Uruguayan has joined a team that loves to defend.

Liverpool hardly ever play cautious football. They embrace a heavy-metal style, which demands intensity, aggressive pressing and immense commitment.

Moreover, Araujo has hardly ever featured in his favoured centre-back position and has instead been converted into a right-back.

Despite everything, the move is working. His physicality, recovery speed and ability to dominate individual duels have become valuable weapons for Liverpool.

His aerial threat has also strengthened Liverpool defensively, an area of the game in which they had struggled prior to his inclusion.

The 27-year-old has won 27 of his first 38 aerial duels this season, while also making 39 clearances.

These numbers are impressive, but Araujo has also revealed that playing regularly has given him the confidence to enjoy his football again.

Araujo looks liberated, and the supporters are embracing every minute of it.

A £47 million decision that suddenly looks more complicated

For all the romanticism surrounding Araujo's revival on Merseyside, Barcelona face a very practical question.

Liverpool have a £47 million (€55 million) option to purchase Araujo permanently at the end of his season-long loan.

A few months ago, Barcelona would have welcomed that outcome with open arms. The club would earn a substantial transfer fee, get huge wages off their books and reinvest that money into a player better suited to Hansi Flick's system.

Pau Cubarsi remains central to Flick's project, while Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen and Gerard Martin provide options in central defence.

That said, what happens if Araujo continues playing like this for the rest of the season?

Liverpool would potentially be signing a player in the prime of his career at an absolute bargain price in the modern market.

Is Araujo's chapter no longer at Barcelona? (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Barcelona, meanwhile, would be surrendering a player who was once considered a cornerstone of their future.

For now, when Araujo was asked about his future, he refused to get carried away. He insisted that it was too early to discuss a permanent move.

However, he did mention that he was very happy and that his family had settled in well on Merseyside.

That is what makes this story bittersweet for Barcelona fans. They once saw Araujo as a player worth building their project around.

Circumstances meant both parties had to part ways for each other's good. Liverpool offered him that opportunity, and now he has endeared himself to a new fanbase.

The sight of Araujo disappearing into the arms of Liverpool supporters captures something pure that no transfer valuation can ever explain.

A player who once wore Barcelona's armband is now slowly becoming one of Liverpool's own. The longer the love affair continues, the further Araujo will slip away from Barça .

His relationship with the English club is one of the most moving feel-good stories so far this season, considering everything he has been through, and long may it continue.

articles.title: El presidente del Ceuta pone su cargo a disposición del club y la afición
articles.standfirst: Luhay Hamido quiere dar un paso al lado tras la derrota ante el Sporting, cuarta consecutiva que le deja como colista
articles.summary: Luhay Hamido quiere dar un paso al lado tras la derrota ante el Sporting, cuarta consecutiva que le deja como colista
articles.body: Tras la dolorosa derrota sufrida por el Ceuta en el Alfonso Murube frente el Sporting de Gijón, cuarta consecutiva y que deja a los caballas como colsitas, el presidente de la entidad Luhay Hamido ha comparecido para anunciar formalmente que pone su cargo a disposición de la junta directiva y de la afición caballa. La decisión llega en un momento delicado en el plano deportivo, marcado por una racha negativa que ha llevado al equipo a ocupar el farolillo rojo de la clasificación. En sus declaraciones, el dirigente blanco no ha ocultado el desgaste personal y emocional acumulado durante los últimos meses. Hamido ha calificado la presente campaña como "un año duro" en todos los sentidos, señalando que ha llegado el momento de replantearse sus prioridades y dedicar más tiempo a su entorno familiar. "Necesito un descanso. Está siendo una etapa muy exigente y la familia requiere ahora mi presencia y mi atención", ha manifestado el máximo mandatario del club. No obstante, Hamido ha querido lanzar un mensaje de tranquilidad sobre la estabilidad institucional del Ceuta. Ha aclarado que, en caso de continuar al frente del proyecto de forma transitoria por no existir un relevo o una alternativa firme, mantendría intacta su confianza en la parcela técnica, contando plenamente con José Juan Romero como entrenador y con Edu Villegas en la dirección deportiva. Pese a garantizar que no dejará a la institución sola ni desamparada ante las dificultades actuales, la postura del presidente marca un punto de inflexión definitivo en el rumbo del club. Hamido ha dejado claro que, se resuelva su salida de forma inmediata o progresiva, el presente ejercicio será, como mínimo, el último bajo su mandato al frente del Ceuta.

articles.title: Lazio pull clear at Serie A summit as Gattuso warns of vertigo
articles.summary: Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A on Sunday with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter Milan after the...
articles.body:
Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A on Sunday with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter Milan after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points.

Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M'Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win.

With 28 points from 10 games, Lazio moved three clear of Inter after they lost the Milan derby. Unbeaten Roma sit third on 24 points and Como climbed back to fourth with a 1-0 win over rock-bottom Venezia.

Lazio last won Serie A in 2000 and this is the best start to a league campaign in the club's history but the Roman outfit's ambitions remain modest according to Gattuso.

"Our target is to avoid relegation and we still need 12 more points," Gattuso said. "We need to get our heads down and work, and not look at the table."

As has been the case in recent home matches, Lazio played in front of largely empty sections of the Stadio Olimpico, with many ultras and supporters continuing their boycott in protest against owner and president Claudio Lotito, whom they accuse of failing to invest sufficiently in the squad.

Como's victory at home over lowly Venezia on Sunday was a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions.

The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. Como captain Lucas Da Cunha converted in the 43rd minute for the French international's first goal of the season.

"This is the type of match we found hard to win last season," Da Cunha told DAZN.

Cesc Fabregas's side had slipped to fifth when AC Milan beat champions Inter 3-1 on Saturday.

Como moved one point behind Roma, who beat Udinese 5-2 on Saturday.

"This victory is really important in terms of our maturing process," said Fabregas.

"Our state of mind is irreproachable," added the 39-year-old Spaniard.

Como resume their Champions League campaign against Lens on Wednesday.

In a season in which Italian teams have struggled in Europe, Como have the best record of the Serie A clubs in the Champions League, sitting ninth in the 36-team standings, with six points from three games.

Como, who were playing in Italy's third division as recently as 2021, beat Manchester United 4-1 in the last round of European matches.

articles.title: Giant curiosity Hibs finally liberated from the sucker punch
articles.summary: Hibernian, for once, avoid late heartbreak to set up League Cup final with Rangers, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
As time ticked on at Hampden, you waited for the Hearts kick to the Hibs solar plexus, the late sickener that became such a huge theme in their clashes last season.

Were Hibs, bottom of the league and incapable of buying a win in recent weeks, really about to beat their city rivals at Hampden for the first time ever? Really?

There were 10 minutes between Hibs and a League Cup final against Rangers, but 10 minutes can be an eternity between these two.

Five minutes left to play now and Hibs still holding a 2-1 lead, but recent history tells us that even five minutes is plenty of time for everything to turn on its head.

Late, late plot twists and late, late Hearts victories came in minutes 86, 88 and 90 in three different Edinburgh derbies last season - all in Hearts' favour, all dropping Hibs to their knees in angst.

Now we were in sniper's alley; two minutes left and Hearts pushing hard.

Hibs edge Hearts in thrilling derby to reach League Cup final

Jordi Altena's delivery from the right finds Claudio Braga, one of the chief dangermen in maroon left all on his lonesome a few yards from goal. Braga's already scored one and is about to score two. Hibs are about to Hibs it all over again. Extra time beckons.

But, no, not this time, not today. Braga blows his big chance. He stands there almost in disbelief. Some of his team-mates are rooted to the spot.

Hibs fans, meanwhile, go berserk. A set of fans hard-bitten by late goals costing them dear this season and last, not just against Hearts, but against Midtjylland and Legia Warsaw, Livingston and Dunfermline, Dundee and Motherwell, Gent and St Mirren, now liberated from the sucker punch.

Free of Hearts' gloating. Joy at last in a season that has brought little more than bitterness and rancour about the state of the club, on the field and off.

Marink Reedijk, their manager, is just in the door. Short of handing the Hibs fans the winning numbers in the lottery there is no greater way for him to endear himself to supporters than beating Hearts. Beating them anywhere, anyhow is special. Beating them in a cup semi-final is extra-special.

Team of contradictions finally makes sense

Hibs are a giant curiosity. Reedijk will know that only too well by now. An enigma. A riddle.

They have good players but they're bottom of the Premiership. They have goal threat but have delivered precious few goals. They have accomplished players in midfield but routinely get bossed in there.

They have plenty of seasoned pros but have lacked bottle. Potential, for sure, but nowhere enough league points and an underdog's tag coming into this semi-final.

Could they put it together on their biggest day of the season so far? After four minutes the answer was an emphatic no. Braga had scored. Easy header. Point blank range. Nobody alive to his menace. Soft. Again.

You didn't write them off at that early stage, but more Hibs things kept happening. Felix Passlack should have scored, but he didn't. Owen Elding should have scored, but he didn't.

Four goals in their past six games, one of them a penalty. No league wins in six. One win in nine - against Ross County from the third tier - in all competitions.

The signs were not good that Hibs would suddenly metamorphose into a convincing, steely bunch of players capable of rolling with the punches instead of being floored by them. But that's what happened.

For the rest of the half, Hibs were terrific, albeit against a Hearts team dropping like flies. Hibs folk will be sick of hearing the chat about the freakish Tynecastle casualty list - Wouter Vrancken isn't exactly loving it either - but it's reality.

The curse struck again in the opening half - a disorientated Tomas Magnusson removed after a horrible clash of heads and then Calvin Miller succumbing to injury and finishing his day with his knee in a brace.

Vrancken intervened on the touchline when it appeared that Magnusson was about to be sent back into the fray. The Hearts manager could see - as anybody who was watching could see - Magnusson clearly unsteady on his feet and wobbling.

Hearts should maybe explain what tests were done on the midfielder and on what basis they decided he was considered fit enough to carry on. Vrancken's alertness and decisiveness may have saved a vulnerable Magnusson a more troubling fate.

Hibs earn moment but has corner been turned?

None of this was Hibs' concern, but it was Hibs' opportunity - and they took it.

Joe Newell found space and dominance in the middle of the park. The organisation and hunger in their press was compelling. Their big players - the ones who have spent far too long playing way below par - found themselves at last.

When Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath scored before the break it was only what Hibs deserved. It was the first time they'd scored twice against Premiership opposition since August.

There is resilience in this Hearts side, though. Braga ought to have scored just before the end of the opening half, a reminder of the wonderful psychology of this fixture. It ain't over until it's over.

Even then, winning the midfield and winning the game, how many would have bet their last fiver on Hibs seeing it out?

This could be a major turning point in their season, so long as Hibs make it so. That's their challenge now. Bottom of the league is ridiculous. They can be - and must be - so much better than that.

Hearts threw everything at them in the second half. They got on top, no question. Hibs became sloppy in those early minutes. Giving away possession easily, inviting Hearts on to them. Again you wondered about Hibs' nerve.

Laurent Mendy lashed one wide, Braga had one saved. Later, Sabri Guendouz had a blast that was tipped over by Raphael Sallinger. Braga had that golden chance at the end.

Hibs always gave Hearts something to think about at the other end, though. They had some counter-attacks and butchered them. Marko Ivezic could have taken away any prospect of a Hearts' revival had he taken a big chance from close range.

It was pulsating stuff. The suspense lasted to the final whistle when Hibs danced their way around Hampden and Sunshine on Leith carried about the stadium. It's been a while since we've heard it. They'd earned their moment.

If it gets another airing next month when Hibs return to face Rangers in the final then a corner will truly have been turned.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta refutes notion that Arsenal's winning visit to Liverpool at Anfield wasn't attacking
articles.summary: Kai Havertz's early goal was enough for the Gunners, but Arteta will know there was plenty of waste from his old pal Andoni Iraola's hosts.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta's Arsenal were under pressure for much of the day but emerged from Anfield with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Liverpool to go alone atop the Premier League table.

Kai Havertz's early goal was enough for the Gunners, but Arteta will know there was plenty of waste from his old pal Andoni Iraola's hosts.

Arteta was not impressed by a question implying that Arsenal had to dig deep and defend despite the Gunners sitting back for much of the game.

Yet a win is a win and the gritty Gunners sank back to ground out these three points.

Mikel Arteta reaction from Arsenal's winning visit to Liverpool at Anfield

Big to get a win at Anfield? "Especially for everybody attached to this football club — 14 years without winning here is a long time. Things happen for a reason and that gave us a belief and a hunger to come here."

That was a slog and not very fluid: "Very fluid at times. We generated six or seven big chances but we couldn't break out. When you misplace a pass or clearance these guys are running at you. Makes it incredible to me."

"They are in a really good moment, had won every game and fully deserved it. To come here and win in the manner that we've done."

Declan Rice's assist was excellent: "The moment to recognize the open situation and timing of him and Noni playing the 2v1. There were other moments where the team had some incredible actions."

articles.title: Havertz becomes EPL's top German scorer in Arsenal win at Liverpool
articles.summary: Kai Havertz’s winning goal in Arsenal’s 1-0 triumph at Liverpool on Sunday made him the record German goalscorer in the Premier League. The Gunners forward s...
articles.body:
Kai Havertz's winning goal in Arsenal's 1-0 triumph at Liverpool on Sunday made him the record German goalscorer in the Premier League.

The Gunners forward surpassed the mark of former Manchester City midfielder İlkay Gündoğan when he tapped home his 46th goal in the competition after 16 minutes at Anfield.

It was his third league strike of the campaign, taking his overall total for the north London club to 27, and sent the champions top of the table after City lost to Brighton on Saturday.

Havertz scored 19 Premier League goals during his spell with Chelsea from 2020 to 2023, a period during which he also netted a Champions League final winner.

Brighton's Pascal Gross is the competition's third most prolific German with 34, ahead of former Arsenal player Mesut Özil with 33.

Other notable Germans on the list include former Tottenham favourite Jürgen Klinsmann with 29 and Michael Ballack, a Chelsea title-winner, with 17.

Havertz's Germany international team-mate Florian Wirtz, who hit the bar for Liverpool, has five goals to his name for the Reds.

articles.title: Cologne's El Mala brothers grab draw at Union, Frankfurt beat Hamburg
articles.summary: Cologne's Malek El Mala scored on his Bundesliga debut to outshine younger brother Saïd and hand his struggling side a 1-1 draw at Union Berlin on Sunday. It...
articles.body:
Cologne's Malek El Mala scored on his Bundesliga debut to outshine younger brother Saïd and hand his struggling side a 1-1 draw at Union Berlin on Sunday.

It was the Billygoats' first away point of the league season. Cologne had thumped Union 5-0 at home in the German Cup second round only on Tuesday.

The El Mala pair shared a pitch for Cologne's senior team for the first time on Sunday as 21-year-old Malek fired into the roof of the net on 79 minutes. His 20-year-old brother's cross had somehow found its way to him across the packed Union box.

"I don't know what to say, it feels unbelievable," Malek told streaming portal DAZN.

"It was a very important for us to get a point. We have really fought and expended lots of energy. But it's all indescribable."

Germany winger Saïd had earlier missed Cologne's best chance up to that point when he shot over, moments after Malek had been introduced from the bench.

The older but less experienced brother showed his sibling how it was done having only been on the field for seven minutes.

Saïd added: "I'm happy for the lad, I see how hard he works. He has totally deserved it."

Union had seized an early lead when Janik Haberer scored his second goal in two games having gone two seasons without netting in the league. The midfielder-turned-wingback prodded home after good work by Tim Skarke.

The capital club are in the relegation play-off spot with seven points from eight games, while Cologne lie 13th on nine.

Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hamburg 3-1 at home in Sunday's late game to leapfrog their 15th-placed opponents and power up to eighth in the tight standings.

Younes Ebnoutalib and Raphael Onyedika struck in the second half to secure the win. Warmed Omari had netted an unlucky own goal on 10 minutes to boost Frankfurt, but Terem Moffi quickly spared his team-mate's blushes with an equalizer.

Frankfurt brought Niko Iličević, the nephew of former Croatia international Ivo Iličević, off the bench for his debut just a day after his 16th birthday.

On Saturday, Borussia Dortmund drew 2-2 at Bayern Munich to stay level on points with the leaders at the top of the Bundesliga.

articles.title: Arsenal win at Liverpool to go three points clear at league summit
articles.summary: Arsenal recorded a first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years but needed some help from Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker, whose first-half error led...
articles.body:
Arsenal recorded a first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years but needed some help from Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker, whose first-half error led to Kai Havertz's solitary goal in the 1-0 win.

Not since manager Mikel Arteta was running the Gunners' midfield in 2012 had they tasted victory in the red half of Merseyside and they were tested to the limit in ending end that run.

However, if it is one thing Arteta's side are well-drilled at it is seeing out games having maximized their opportunities and the celebrations in front of the visiting fans having moved top of the table showed how significant they felt this result was.

And while most of the football was played by Liverpool after going behind it did not bring any rewards – partly due to poor judgement and execution but also bad luck.

How Jurrien Timber's tug on the shirt of Alexander Isak as he tried to connect with a header escaped the eagle eye of VAR will remain a question, especially as they were quick to look into a more regular coming together of Cody Gakpo and Christos Tzolis.

By then the hosts were already behind after another miscalculation by Alisson.

A week ago against Brighton the Brazil international had got away with a few loose passes in the win against Brighton. Arsenal were not so forgiving.

His attempted pass to Jeremy Jacquet gave the centre-back no chance of retaining possession and the loose ball was seized upon by Arsenal, who moved it the right where Noni Madueke and Declan Rice combined for Havertz to tap in at the far post.

The margins were always going to be tight in a match between the current champions, who have won all five league games when scoring the game's first this season, and their predecessors and that one error proved to be the difference as for all their pressure Liverpool failed to test David Raya.

Much of that was down to the hosts' lack of composure in the final third – Raya did not have to make a save – and Arsenal's experience at doing the necessary dirty work to deny those opportunities.

articles.title: Rice rewarded, Wirtz must do more - Liverpool and Arsenal player ratings
articles.summary: How Liverpool and Arsenal's players rated in their Premier League match at Anfield, as the champions of the past two seasons went head to head.
articles.body:
Kai Havertz's first-half goal made the difference as Arsenal won at Anfield in the Premier League for the first time since 2012.

Here's how we rated the Liverpool and Arsenal players, and your scores are below.

Alisson: It was his error - a poor pass out - that led to Havertz giving Arsenal the lead. Made a great save to deny Christos Tzolis but that mistake ultimately proved costly. 4

Ronald Araujo : Made his 12th consecutive start. Battled well as ever but was given a really tough test by Tzolis down Arsenal's left. 6

Jeremy Jacquet : Shaky in patches but had a decent game on the whole and made a superb tackle after slipping in the second half. 6

Virgil van Dijk : Reliable as ever but will be so disappointed with how easily Liverpool gifted Arsenal the lead. 6

Milos Kerkez : Had a frustrating first half but delivered a lovely cross which Alexis Mac Allister should have headed in. 5

Trey Nyoni : A real show of faith from Andoni Iraola to give the 19-year-old his first Premier League start. Looked a bit nervy early on but grew into the game. 6

Alexis Mac Allister : Constantly involved in the first half but will know that he should have scored when Kerkez found him. 6

Bradley Barcola : Started down his preferred left flank and caused Arsenal plenty of problems, though he is still waiting for a first Premier League goal. 7

Florian Wirtz : Hit the bar with a great free-kick in the first half, but a player with his price tag simply has to do more in big games. 6

Cody Gakpo : Looked lively initially, but Riccardo Calafiori dealt with him very well. Could have had a penalty, but the appeal was waved away by Andy Madley. 5

Alexander Isak : Got in some good positions but couldn't find the net. Unlucky not to get a penalty when his shirt was pulled by Timber. 5

Szoboszlai (on 59, Nyoni): Back after a spell on the sidelines. 6

Ngumoha (on 67, Gakpo): Didn't get on the ball as much as he would have liked. 5

Munoz (on 82, Araujo): Tried to make an impact with his pace.

Koumas (on 82, Wirtz): Thrown on to add some energy.

Tsimikas (on 82, Kerkez): Didn't have much luck down the left.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Endo, Gravenberch.

David Raya: Made a good clearance after a ball was played through the Arsenal defence in the first half. The usual assured performance from the goalkeeper. 7

Jurrien Timber: Involved in a very good battle with Barcola and had to deal with a lot of attacks down the right side. Perhaps lucky to not give away a penalty for a shirt pull on Isak. 7

Ezri Konsa: Continued his recent good form and was solid in the middle of the Arsenal back four. 8

Gabriel Magalhaes: Dealt with the threat of Isak and led the Arsenal backline. 8

Riccardo Calafiori: Not allowed to attack as much as usual but a solid defensive performance from the left-back. 8

Declan Rice: The midfielder provided the assist for Havertz's goal and was Arsenal's best player. His energy in midfield was a big reason the Gunners won the game. 8

Bruno Guimaraes: An all-action display and involved in the move for the Arsenal goal. Subbed just after an hour. 6

Martin Odegaard: Won the ball back which started the move for the Arsenal opener. 6

Noni Madueke: Heavily involved in the opening goal as he started after shaking off a knock. Tired as the game went on. 6

Christos Tzolis: The winger's first start since September after injury and provided a threat from the left. Forced Alisson into an excellent save with a curling effort. 6

Kai Havertz: Scored the only goal of the game, which he needed after a difficult couple of matches. Put himself about and linked the play. 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly (on 62, Guimaraes): Came on and helped to calm the game down for Arsenal as Liverpool pushed for an equaliser. 7

Piero Hincapie (on 84, Tzolis): Brought on to see out the win. 6

Viktor Gyokeres (on 84, Havertz): Introduced to provide a threat behind the backline. 6

Merino (on 88, Odegaard): Added defensive strength for the closing minutes.

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, Mosquera, White, Eze, Zubimendi.

articles.body:
San Mamés hosts a thrilling edition of the Basque derby between Athletic Club and Real Sociedad this Sunday on Matchday 11 of LaLiga.

Edin Terzic's Lions head into the game with renewed confidence after back-to-back emphatic wins over Getafe (4-0) and AE Prat (1-6), powered by the game-changing talents of Nico and Iñaki Williams. On the other side, the in-form San Sebastián outfit arrive with four consecutive league wins and a six-match unbeaten run, with a brilliant Mikel Oyarzabal leading the attack, as they look to extend their five-match unbeaten streak against their fierce rivals in competitive meetings.
